scope: Batches 11–12, 20 meanings and 60 offline question bands

items.meaning: getting heated; growing excited while speaking
items.reviewNote: In chapter IV 103:62, échauffant means getting heated; growing excited while speaking. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The reflexive gerund describes increasing animation while speaking, rather than physical warming by an external heat source.

In chapter IV 103:89, cassé means broken; snapped. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The snapped necklace thread causes the diamonds to fall; the completed participle has masculine singular agreement with fil.

In chapter IV 103:98, fil means thread; string holding the necklace. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Only the literal thread at unit 103:98 is assigned. Fil at unit 95:216 remains a held component of de droit fil.

In chapter IV 104:13, tombèrent means fell; dropped. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 104:38, jolis means pretty; attractive. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 104:51, carats means small diamonds sold by weight. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The 1762 Académie entry also calls small diamonds sold by weight carats; the passage says these carats fell and weighed many livres, so the noun refers to the stones themselves, not only the unit.

In chapter IV 104:64, inégaux means unequal; of different sizes. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 104:92, pesaient means weighed; had a weight of. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Literal mass in livres differs from the published figurative burden sense of peser.

In chapter IV 105:19, quelques-uns means some of them. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The indefinite pronoun identifies several but not all diamonds; link to the earlier feminine quelques-unes pronoun sense while retaining this masculine form’s questions.

In chapter IV 105:126, taillés means cut; faceted. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source explicitly connects the diamonds’ cut to their usefulness as microscopes, so this is faceting rather than pruning or resizing clothing.

In chapter IV 105:145, excellents means excellent; very good. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Both indexed uses qualify the improvised optical instruments as very good.

items.meaning: microscope; instrument for viewing tiny things
items.reviewNote: In chapter IV 106:22, microscope means microscope; instrument for viewing tiny things. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Both singular uses of the optical instrument share the earlier planned plural microscopes sense.

In chapter IV 106:75, appliqua means placed against; applied. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 106:89, prunelle means pupil of the eye. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The 1762 Académie anatomy entry identifies the dark opening in the eye; all Level 4–5 alternatives are feminine singular eye parts.

In chapter IV 106:117, choisit means chose; selected. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

items.meaning: to adjust oneself; align the eye
items.reviewNote: In chapter IV 107:85, ajuster means to adjust oneself; align the eye. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The reflexive infinitive in the optical scene means aligning one’s viewing position for the instrument.

In chapter IV 108:66, remuait means was moving; stirring. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 108:125, baleine means whale; large marine mammal. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Both singular source uses refer to the animal seen through the optical instrument; feminine singular distractors are other sea creatures.

In chapter IV 109:36, adroitement means deftly; skillfully. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 109:70, ongle means fingernail. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The anatomical fingernail matches the published sense; the middle prompt distinguishes it from the entire thumb or arm.
